title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az interface endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Added Terraform modules and Helm hooks to provision multi-AZ VPC networking for the private control plane: subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. No API changes. Requires env variable TF_VAR_privatelink_enabled for enabling interface endpoints in existing installs.
description: Context: Private deployments require a hardened VPC control plane with multi-AZ subnets, AWS interface endpoints for AWS-managed services, strict control-plane security groups, and support for cross-account peering with delegated Route53 zones. This PR adds a set of Terraform modules and orchestration knobs to provision multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 forwarding/delegation records. Motivation: simplify on-prem/VPC installs, reduce manual post-provision steps in the installer, and enable safe automated upgrades/rollouts for network resources. What changed: added modules/network/vpc-control-plane (multi-az subnet templates, AZ placement), modules/network/interface_endpoints (S3, STS, EC2API, KMS optional), modules/network/peering (cross-account peering + route propagation), modules/dns/route53-delegation (private hosted zone delegation with cross-account role), updated helm chart templates to include pre-upgrade and post-rollback hooks that mark network changes as applied, added tfvars examples and upgrade hooks in private-installer/README. Upgrade notes: terraform plan must be reviewed for existing customers; interface endpoints are opt-in (TF_VAR_privatelink_enabled=false by default) to avoid accidental creation in accounts that restrict endpoint creation. Rollback strategy: modules are tolerant to destroy on rollback; peering and delegation resources include lifecycle rules and explicit dependencies to avoid orphaned DNS records. Testing: applied to staging account (us-west-2) with three AZs and to a partner integration account for cross-account peering. Smoke tests: control-plane components registered successfully, DNS resolution validated for delegated zone, endpoint connectivity tested against S3 and STS. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserved (no endpoints created unless opted-in). Related: linear ENG-1987, ops runbook update in PR #540128. Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules added and documented - [x] Helm hooks for upgrade/rollback included - [x] Staging apply and smoke tests passed - [x] Security review for SG rules completed - [x] Release notes drafted

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Overall looks good. Can we make the interface endpoints opt-in by default? I don't want surprises in existing customer accounts.
Ava Thompson: Yes, endpoints are opt-in via TF_VAR_privatelink_enabled=false by default. Updated variables.tf and docs to highlight this.
Li Wei: The SG rules look permissive for the control-plane-to-worker path. Can we scope by prefix-list and ensure no 0.0.0.0/0 egress?
Ava Thompson: Adjusted SGs to reference customer_subnet_prefix_lists and added explicit egress to AWS-managed prefixes only; updated test cases.
Riley Patel: Please add a safety check in the peering module to prevent accidental peering into production accounts.
Ava Thompson: Added an allowed_peer_accounts variable with validation and explicit acceptance step in README.
CI bot: terraform fmt/lint failed on first run - fixed formatting and re-ran.
Diego Martinez: Approved after final fixes.
merge_outcome: merged by Li Wei after approvals and green CI. Release window scheduled for 2024-05-21.
notes: Operational: Operators must set TF_VAR_privatelink_enabled=true to enable interface endpoints when running private-installer against existing VPCs. For cross-account peering, ensure the peer account grants the delegation role described in modules/dns/route53-delegation/README. See private-installer/README for rollback steps and known limitations.
